question.problem: Which of the following is the best estimate for $\sqrt{29}?$
question.worked_solution:
To estimate $\sqrt{29},$ we first find the two perfect squares closest to $29.$

The closest perfect squares are $25={5}^{2}$ and $36={6}^{2}.$

Since $25<29<36,$ we know that the square root of $29$ lies between $5$ and $6.$ This tells us that $4.9$ and $14.5$ are incorrect estimates.

Because $29$ is much closer to $25$ than to $36$ (the distance to $25$ is $4,$ and the distance to $36$ is $7$), we expect $\sqrt{29}$ to be near the lower end of the interval.

We can test the plausible choices by squaring them to see which one results in a value closest to $29:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5.4}^{2} & =29.16 \\ {5.7}^{2} & =32.49 \\ {5.9}^{2} & =34.81\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${5.4}^{2}=29.16$ is very close to $29.$

Therefore, the best estimate for $\sqrt{29}$ is $5.4.$
